Primarily, a significant amount of Page32 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version electricity is needed to power the liquefaction process where the compressors that compress the CO gas 2 in three stages are by far the largest consumer of electricity. Aptamus and its technical consultant Entr have had several meetings with TECO personnel during the study period, and TECO has confirmed that it is able and willing to provide new power transmission infrastructure as necessary to satisfy T-RICH’s power demands. In those meetings, TECO and Entr agreed that the optimum supply voltage would be 69 kV. Other details were discussed but not yet finalized because laying new power lines and associated equipment from outside the fence line of the T-RICH site is not within the scope of this study. Some outstanding issues for future study, however, include 1) whether power would come from an existing or new substation, or from a tap on an existing transmission line, 2) whether Aptamus or TECO will provide the switchgear, and 3) whose specifications would govern the switchgear design. Additionally, we intend to evaluate whether a solar energy generation system could reduce the cost of the TECO-supplied electricity, thereby reducing the overall OPEX of the T-RICH site. The T-RICH hub will consume a relatively small amount of water, and generate only a small amount of sewage from its administrative building and workshop. PTB’s subcontractor confirmed that existing potable water and sewer lines run down Pendola Point Road, along the south edge of the T-RICH hub site. The potable water line is 8 inches in diameter, and a new 2-inch branch line will be connected with a tapping valve and sleeve and run to the administrative building with a 2-inch isolation valve, a water meter, and a backflow preventer. In addition, a new 6-inch line will be tapped off the existing 8-inch city line to be run to a new fire hydrant in the middle of the hub. A 2-inch HDPE force main will be installed from the administration building back to the existing 8-inch force main at the street. Sewage will be run through an E/One DH071 Grinder Pump Station to ensure adequate pressure.See Figure 3.13 for a snip of the Utility Plan. Tampa Bay includes several Aquatic Preserves managed by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, including the Pinellas, Boca Ciega Bay, Terra Ceia and Cockroach Bay Aquatic Preserves.
